subject: Enclave-wrapped BYO keyflow and network fencing for Private/VPC deployment
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Cc: acme-security-team@example.com
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deploy: BYOK with enclave wrapping + egress constraints

Marissa —

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. To recap our security team asks for the Redwood Private deployment we're evaluating:

- BYOK support using our HSM-backed master keys (we need a model for wrapping the tenant key so we never upload unwrapped tenant material into your control plane).
- Optional enclave-based unwrapping (we'd prefer the unwrapping to occur inside a sealed SGX-like enclave or equivalent).
- Strong egress restrictions: proxied outbound only to specific telemetry endpoints; no raw model tokens leave the VPC unencrypted.
- Rotation cadence for ephemeral wrapping keys (we'd like a recommended cadence and a safe rollback/forensic path).
- Audit evidence we can include in our internal intake (logs, KMS audit trail, signing of CSR exchanges).

I attached our short KMS requirements doc. Can you sketch how Redwood would wire BYOK+enclave+network-fencing for an on-prem/private VPC install? High level diagram and a short list of operational assumptions would be perfect.

Oliver
Security Lead, Acme Corp

Attachment: acme_kms_requirements.docx (docx, 78KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 12:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Private deploy: BYOK with enclave wrapping + egress constraints

Oliver —

Appreciate the clear ask and the doc. I ran this by Jonas and Karthik; below is a high-level design we propose for Acme's Private deployment. Keeping it concise so you can circulate to your security reviewers.

Design summary (high level):
1) Key onboarding: Acme provides a wrapped tenant root (TRK) using your HSM. We support two patterns: a) offline hardware-wrapped TRK (you provide an encrypted blob and attestation), or b) remote HSM proxy where your HSM issues short-lived wrapping tokens.

2) Enclave unwrapping: The encrypted TRK is only unwrapped inside a hardened enclave on customer-controlled hosts (Redwood private runtime deployed into your VPC). The enclave performs final key-material import into an in-memory, ephemeral keystore; nothing at rest in plaintext.

3) Ephemeral KEKs: The runtime generates ephemeral Key-Encrypting-Keys (KEKs) per node / per epoch, which are themselves wrapped with the TRK. KEKs are rotated automatically (configurable cadence).

4) Egress fencing: Network policies limit outbound to:
   - Redwood telemetry collector endpoints (TLS + mTLS)
   - Vault/KMS remote proxies (if using remote HSM proxy)
   - Customer-approved package repo endpoints (for updates)
No other outbound connections are permitted from the enclave host by default.

5) Audit and evidence: The enclave attestation report, import logs, and KMS wrap/unwrap events are shipped to an internal audit bucket you own (S3/GCS in your account) and to your SIEM over a controlled channel.

Attachments: I attached a very small diagram (redwood-private-enclave-draft-v1.pdf) and a short list of suggested rotation defaults.

Can we schedule a 45-minute technical deep-dive tomorrow? Jonas can cover the runtime and KMS flow details.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-private-enclave-draft-v1.pdf (pdf, 112KB)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acme-corp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 09:38:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Private deploy: BYOK with enclave wrapping + egress constraints

Oliver / team —

Dropping a few concrete operational notes so we can make the deep-dive productive:

Operational model (concrete):
- Import flow: Acme generates TRK in your HSM -> wrap with Redwood import key (customer-side tooling) -> upload wrapped blob to a customer-owned import bucket. The import API requires a signed request (mutual TLS) and an attestation document signed by the enclave.

- Enclave lifecycle:
  * Enclave boots on host; generates local ephemeral KEK (KEK_node_v1) -> enclave requests attestation nonce -> Redwood attestation verifier (deployed in your control plane) verifies measurement -> enclave performs TRK unwrap.
  * KEKs are rotated per-node every 24 hours by default; configurable to 6/12/24h. Rotation triggers material re-wrapping and a small grace window during rollout for live inference keys.

- Rollback & forensics:
  * We retain wrap/unwrap event logs and nonce/attestation artifacts in your audit bucket for 90 days (configurable).
  * If you revoke a TRK, runtime will reject KEK unwraps and can return encrypted snapshots for offline forensics.

- Offline HSM option: If you prefer a fully offline import ceremony, we have a documented operator playbook: sealed import token -> local operator uploads -> verifier performs a batched attestation verification. This minimizes exposure of TRK during transit.

- Network lockdown specifics:
  * Egress rule set (example): allow TCP 443 to telemetry.redwood.example:443 (mTLS), allow to acme-s3-bucket endpoints, allow to your HSM proxy IPs. Block DNS to public resolvers by default (use your internal recursive DNS).

If this maps to your needs we can finalize the diagram and an operator checklist for your runbook.

— Jonas
Principal Applied Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Cc: acme-security-team@example.com, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deploy: BYOK with enclave wrapping + egress constraints

Thanks Jonas — that level of detail is exactly what our reviewers needed. A couple follow-ups before we lock to an operator run: 

1) Evidence: can the attestation reports and the wrap/unwrap audit be pushed to our SIEM (Splunk) via a signed webhook to a private collector? We want tamper-evident delivery.
2) Time sync: is there a recommended clock-drift tolerance for nonce validation? Our infra runs in multiple DCs, some with intermittent NTP availability.
3) CA/TLS: do you support customer-provided CA bundles for mutual TLS, or does Redwood require Redwood-managed certs for the telemetry channel?

Once we confirm these three items I'd like to open a short procurement packet and schedule the operator cutover rehearsal next week.

Oliver

On a related note: any SOC2 evidence you can provide about your enclave attestation verification process will speed internal approval.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 09:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Private deploy: BYOK with enclave wrapping + egress constraints

Oliver —

Short answers and next steps: 

1) Evidence delivery: yes — we can push signed, timestamped attestation artifacts to your Splunk collector using an mTLS webhook. Events are batched with sequence numbers and HMAC signing at the source; we will provide the signing key exchange as part of the runbook.

2) Time sync: nonce validation defaults to +/- 5 minutes. For intermittent NTP we recommend a 10-minute tolerance and persisting nonces for replay detection during short disconnect windows. We'll include configuration knobs in the operator checklist.

3) CA/TLS: we support customer-provided CA bundles for all mutual TLS channels. For telemetry we can either use Redwood-managed certs (short-lived) or your CA; most customers choose their CA for Private deployments.

Action items: 
- Jonas to produce an operator checklist + verified diagram (target: EOD Mon 22 Feb).
- Marissa to deliver a sample Splunk ingestion config and webhook signing spec (target: Tue 23 Feb).
- Acme to confirm preferred rotation cadence (24h default) and supply the HSM contact for proxy option.

I'll create a short runbook draft and share a Drive link once Jonas drops the checklist. Thanks — looking forward to the rehearsal.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
